name: Facet
text:
Build the live-coded HTML/CSS demo. It proves real speed by letting users interact with actual performance, not a polished illusion. The trade-off is less visual polish upfront, but we avoid fooling ourselves—and users—into thinking a Figma prototype is fast when it’s just responsive.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Figma’s polished demo still risks users mistaking the prototype for the real thing—confusing "feels fast" with "is fast." A live-coded demo risks exposing half-baked UX before the core flow is locked, but the real risk is users judging speed by janky interactions, not actual performance. Settle it by A/B testing both: measure how often users confuse prototype speed for real speed, and track which artifact uncovers more UX gaps.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship a minimal, live-coded HTML/CSS demo of Excava’s core flow—no Figma, no polish—so users can *break* it in real time and feel real speed, not the illusion of it. Own it: Facet.
